Laura —

Quick note from infra after an initial capacity check:

- The Dedicated pool has ~1,800 A100-equivalent slots running nominally. Unallocated buffer currently at ~9% (~160 slots) after existing commitments.
- To support Acme's 120-slot ask by Apr 15, we'd need to: 1) defer two low-priority burst pools (client-facing POCs) and 2) shift one tranche of our scheduled maintenance (targeting Apr 12) to Apr 19. That gives us the capacity but reduces our contingency buffer to ~2%.
- Alternative: provision 80 guaranteed slots + 40 burst-eligible slots (soft isolation) — lowers immediate stress and keeps contingency at ~6%.

Blockers: procurement timeline for Acme's contract (they requested custom data retention controls) — if Legal/Procurement can't clear the agreement by Apr 10 we can't expose the reserved slots. Also, we need a finance confirmation on spending runway for the first 60 days.

I'll make a short runbook change to document the maintenance shift and the soft-burst approach.

—Karthik
Head of Infra Operations

From Sales-finance perspective:

- If we go with Karthik's hybrid (80 guaranteed + 40 burst) we can model initial spend for 60 days at ~$78k/mo incremental run-rate (GPU + networking + storage amortized). That keeps the deal economics intact for Acme (they accept a 10% pilot discount).
- Full 120 guaranteed starts at Apr 15 would add ~120k/mo and needs approval from Finance lead (I'm copying Marissa). We can cover the first monthly delta from our deal-level commit (deal reserves) but Finance wants to formalize a 90-day runway and clawback mechanism in case utilization is below 50%.

Actionable: Sales will ask Acme procurement to confirm a signed SOW by Apr 08. If they push past that date we should default to the hybrid tranche and schedule the capacity increase for May 1.
